summary: The Archive screen (portale.html markup 2186-2232) is a paginated table of "intelligence captures": date, type, item title + crop/region subtitle, source, and a "CONNECTED TO" column, plus a text query, four dropdown filters (type / crop / region / company), nine coloured type chips with counts, and a right-hand drawer with a summary paragraph, crop/issue/region tags and up to six cross-links (opportunity, future signal, ADAMA product, competitor, source, research topic). Today every fact on that screen comes from window.ITALY_DEMO.ARCHIVE: 448 rows, of which 420 are procedurally generated in italy-demo-data.js lines 522-538 (type, source route, company, product, caseObj, signal and an English prose summary are all synthesised from a modulo over the demo CASES/SIGNALS arrays) and only 28 are real (news + bulletins + science re-shaped at lines 539-543). The screen also feeds the nav badge (line 2608, K.archive = 448), the Data-State panel Archive row (line 2530), the Source-detail "LATEST CAPTURES · N IN ARCHIVE" block (line 3368, markup 2311-2312) and the global search ARCHIVE group (line 3383). The real replacement, APP.collections.archive, already exists and holds 740 rows derived from the normalized collections, but it is currently dead code — declared as A_ARCHIVE0 at line 2467 and never read.
realSource: window.ITALY_APP_MODEL.collections.archive (740 records, provenance REAL_DERIVED), built in italy-app-model.js lines 266-276 as an index over scienceRecords (88, from IG.SCIENCE), marketObservations (77, from IG.MARKET), competitorActivities (503, from IG.COMP_ACTIVITIES), voices (17, from IG.VOICES), events (18, from IG.EVENTS), news (8, from IG.NEWS) and windows (29, from ITALY_CANONICAL.windows). Measured: 740 rows, 740 unique ids, 0 duplicate ids, 0 null ids; provenance is REAL_SOURCE (711) or CANONICAL (29) — zero synthetic rows.

modelChanges.why: Fix six measured field-mapping bugs in the push() calls at italy-app-model.js lines 269-275. They silently null or corrupt fields the Archive screen renders. These are not new facts — the data is already in ITALY_INGEST and is simply being read under the wrong key.
modelChanges.derivation: SCIENCE date: line 269 passes r.date||r.year, but scienceRecords maps date from r.DATE||r.date and IG.SCIENCE has neither — the real field is PUBLISHED_AT (measured 88/88 non-null, e.g. '2024-04-01'). Result today: 88/88 SCIENCE rows have date null. Fix scienceRecords to read S(r.PUBLISHED_AT). — EVENT title: line 273 passes e.name, mapped from e.NAME||e.name; IG.EVENTS field is EVENT (measured 18/18 non-null, e.g. 'EIMA International 2026'). Result today: 18/18 EVENT rows have title null. — EVENT url: mapped from e.URL||e.url; the real field is OFFICIAL_URL (18/18). Also line 273 passes e.location as the SOURCE column, so the source reads 'BolognaFiere, Bologna' / 'Piemonte'; use ORGANIZER (5 distinct, 18/18) as source and keep LOCATION as a separate location field. — NEWS source: line 274 passes n.outlet, mapped from n.OUTLET||n.outlet||n.SOURCE; the real field is PUBLISHER (8/8). Result today: 8/8 NEWS rows show a blank SOURCE cell. — NEWS url: mapped from n.URL||n.url; the real field is SOURCE_URL (8/8). — MARKET crop: line 270 passes m.product as the crop. IG.MARKET.PRODUCT is a price-series code ('BLTPAN|PAN', 'MAI|FEED', 'DUR|UNKNOWN', 'Extra virgin olive oil (up to 0.8%)'), not a crop. It injects 12 non-crop values into the crop filter over 77 rows. Set crop = null and expose the code as archive.series instead. — COMPETITOR crop: line 271 passes (a.crops||[])[0]; measured values include the generic Italian words 'colture' (29 rows), 'cereali' (19), 'frutta' (3) alongside Latin binomials. Keep them but tag the vocabulary (see next entry) so the filter does not present them as crop keys.

modelChanges.why: The view needs a stable source join. Today archive.source is a free-text display label mixing four different vocabularies (institution names like 'University of Verona', registry codes like 'IT-SRC-AGRIFOOD', platform names like 'META_ADS_LIBRARY'/'YOUTUBE', and event venue strings like 'Rimini Expo Centre, Rimini') — 21 distinct values. The aSource filter and the Source-detail cross-link (line 3368) cannot work against it.
modelChanges.derivation: sourceId, derived only from real per-record source fields, never guessed: SCIENCE -> r.SOURCE_ID (measured: all 88 = 'IT-SRC-OPENALEX'); MARKET -> m.SOURCE_ID (all 77 = 'IT-SRC-AGRIFOOD'); VOICE -> v.SOURCE_ID (all 17 = 'IT-SRC-YOUTUBE'); COMPETITOR -> from a.platform, META_ADS_LIBRARY (414) -> 'IT-SRC-META', YOUTUBE (89) -> 'IT-SRC-YOUTUBE' (both platforms are registered sources in IG.SOURCES); NEWS -> exact match of n.PUBLISHER against IG.SOURCES[].NAME, which resolves 6 of 8 ('AgroNotizie (Image Line)'->IT-SRC-PROBE-003, 'ADAMA Italia'x2->IT-SRC-PROBE-020, 'Bayer Crop Science Italia'->IT-SRC-PROBE-019, "L'Informatore Agrario"->IT-SRC-PROBE-002, 'Terra e Vita (Edagricole)'->IT-SRC-PROBE-001) and leaves 2 null ('Agronotizie' unnormalized, 'Consorzio Fitosanitario di Modena' vs registry name 'Consorzio Fitosanitario Provinciale di Modena') — leave those null, do not fuzzy-match; EVENT -> null (18, no SOURCE_ID upstream); WINDOW -> null (29; ITALY_CANONICAL.windows[].SOURCE_IDS is measured empty for all 29). Total coverage 691/740 = 93.4%. sourceName = the matching IG.SOURCES[].NAME, else null.

modelChanges.why: The 'CONNECTED TO' column, the drawer link list and the aCase/aCompany filters need explicit relation keys instead of the demo's caseObj/signal/product/company object graph.
modelChanges.derivation: company = a.company for COMPETITOR rows only (measured 503/503 non-null, 11 distinct: BASF 138, FMC 102, Corteva 94, Bayer 86, Syngenta 55, UPL 13, Sipcam 6, Certis 4, Gowan 2, Sumitomo 2, Nufarm 1); null for all other kinds. legacyCaseId = w.LEGACY_CASE_ID for WINDOW rows only (measured 29/29 non-null, exactly one row per IT-OPP-001..029); null for all other kinds — no other collection carries a case link, and IG.OPPORTUNITIES/IG.FUTURE_SIGNALS SOURCE_IDS are source-registry ids, measured 0 of 15 matching any archive record id. competitorProducts = a.products for COMPETITOR (102/503 non-empty) — these are COMPETITOR products, never ADAMA products.

modelChanges.why: Dates arrive in five incompatible shapes and 219 rows have none. Presentation may sort and compute days from supplied dates (§7) but must not invent them, and the list currently has no sort at all (it is in push order, kind by kind).
modelChanges.derivation: Keep date as the raw upstream string for display. Add dateISO = the value only when it already parses as YYYY-MM-DD, plus MARKET's DD/MM/YYYY (40 rows) converted mechanically. Measured shapes over 740: ISO 457, DD/MM/YYYY 40 (IG.MARKET.PUBLICATION_DATE), literal 'NAO SEI' 18 (17 VOICE + 1), range '2026-11-10 a 2026-11-14' 5 (EVENT), '2026-08/09' 1, null 219. After the SCIENCE PUBLISHED_AT fix above, null drops to 131 and dateISO coverage rises to 545/740 = 73.6%. dateState = 'EXACT' | 'RANGE' | 'PERIOD' | 'UNKNOWN' (the 18 'NAO SEI' rows are UNKNOWN, not a date). daysFromRef = AM.daysFrom(dateISO) using APP.referenceDate 2026-09-02 only — no new Date().

modelChanges.why: Vocabulary honesty for the crop filter. The 47 distinct crop values are five mutually unintelligible vocabularies and must not be presented as one dropdown of crop keys.
modelChanges.derivation: cropVocab = 'CANONICAL' for the 29 WINDOW rows (English canonical names: Grapevine, Maize, Olive, Sugar Beet, Apple, Wheat, Durum Wheat, Tomato, Rice, Soybean), 'UPPER_CODE' for SCIENCE/VOICE/NEWS (OLIVE, VINE, DURUM_WHEAT, MAIS, MAIZE, CEREAL...), 'LATIN' for the COMPETITOR rows whose crops[0] is a binomial (Vitis vinifera 42, Zea mays 59, Olea europaea 12, Solanum lycopersicum 4, Helianthus annuus 5, Malus domestica 3, Beta vulgaris 1, Oryza sativa 1, Citrus 5), 'GENERIC_IT' for the COMPETITOR rows whose crops[0] is a generic Italian word (colture 29, cereali 19, frutta 3), and null where crop is null (401/740 non-null, so 339 rows have no crop at all). The engineer must NOT map these onto each other — that is upstream normalization work, not a view fix.

modelChanges.why: Presentation metadata only (§4). Legacy typeColor is measured to be the single constant '#B1A9A7' on all 448 demo rows, so nothing informational is lost by moving colour under .ui.
modelChanges.derivation: A hardcoded per-kind map in the model: { COMPETITOR, SCIENCE, MARKET, WINDOW, EVENT, VOICE, NEWS } -> { color, order }. Not derived from any record; pure layout. This is the one archive field allowed to be authored rather than ingested.

modelChanges.why: Optional but cheap insurance for id collisions in the next intelligence package.
modelChanges.derivation: recordKey = kind + ':' + id. Today ids are already globally unique (measured 740 unique of 740, 0 duplicates, 0 nulls), so this is not required for correctness now — but the archive is a union of seven independently-numbered upstream sequences and nothing upstream guarantees that stays true. Use recordKey for state.archiveId; keep .id for display and deep links.

fieldsThatDie.usedAt: portale.html 3318 (aRegion filter clause), markup 2195 (region <select>), markup 2210 (row subtitle '{{ a.cropL }} · {{ a.region }}'), markup 2223 (drawer region tag), markup 2312 (source-detail row subtitle), 3383 (search match string)
fieldsThatDie.note: This is the biggest loss and it must not be softened. Measured: 0 of 740 real archive rows carry a region, and only 29 (3.9%) can get one at all — the canonical WINDOW rows, whose REGION is one of 9 Italian regions. Everything else has nothing usable: all 17 IG.VOICES.REGION are the literal string 'NAO SEI'; all 8 IG.NEWS.REGION are 'NAO SEI'; IG.COMP_ACTIVITIES has only country ('IT' or null) with the explicit countrySem warning 'AD_REACHED_COUNTRY != AD_TARGETED_COUNTRY'; all 77 IG.MARKET.GEOGRAPHY are 'IT — praca nomeada'; all 88 IG.SCIENCE.COUNTRY_OF_FACT are 'IT'; IG.EVENTS.LOCATION is a venue string, not the region of a fact. Delete the region <select> at line 2195, delete the aRegion state key and its filter clause, delete the drawer region tag, and replace the '· {{ a.region }}' half of the two row subtitles with '· {{ a.issueL }}' (issue is present on 240/740). Do not substitute country 'IT' for region — that would turn a country into a region claim, and for competitor rows it would additionally breach §9.

No real equivalent exists. The 420 demo summaries are template prose generated at italy-demo-data.js line 536 ('Regional bulletin item reporting X situation on Y in Z, with crop stage and monitoring guidance.') — pure invention. What reality has instead is three different things with three different meanings, covering 417/740 = 56.4%: IG.NEWS.SINTONIA_SUMMARY (8, a Sintonia-written précis), IG.VOICES.WHAT_IT_PROVES / WHAT_IT_DOES_NOT_PROVE (17, an evidence verdict), and IG.COMP_ACTIVITIES.text (392 of 503, raw ad copy that must not be translated per §11). Replace the single prose block with a per-kind evidence block that names what it is showing, and render nothing for SCIENCE (88), MARKET (77), EVENT (18) and WINDOW (29). Do not synthesize a sentence to fill the gap and do not redesign the drawer to hide the emptiness (§3).

risks: The archive count on the nav badge goes UP (448 -> 740) while the screen gets visibly thinner: no region column content, no summary paragraph on 323 rows, an empty CONNECTED TO cell on 711 rows. Someone will read that as a regression. It is the opposite — 420 of the old 448 rows were fabricated. Say so before the review, not after.

The 29 WINDOW rows are the ONLY rows with a region and the ONLY rows with a case link, and they are also the least document-like rows in the set: ITALY_CANONICAL.windows[].PROVENANCE is measured 'EXPECTED_NORM', they have no url (29/29 null), and their source reads the literal 'CANONICAL'. Any feature rebuilt on them (a region facet, a per-case evidence list) would be resting an observational claim on an expected agronomic norm. Decide deliberately whether they belong in an archive of captures at all.

The crop filter is a correctness trap. If line 2194 keeps reading the shared {{ cropOptions }} prop, the UI will silently look fine and return at most 5 rows for any crop — a wrong-looking-right failure, the worst kind. This must be caught in the same commit that touches the model, not later.

COMPETITOR rows are 503 of 740 = 68% of the archive. Sorting by date newest-first will make the first pages almost entirely Meta ad records, and the '2026-01-30'-style start dates are ad campaign starts, not publication dates of an observation. Do not let the date column imply 'when this was observed'. Also §9: an archive row must not inherit REACHED_IN_ITALY framing from its geoClass.

archive.source is a display label mixing four vocabularies; if the engineer wires the aSource filter to it instead of the new sourceId, the filter will half-work (it will match 'YOUTUBE' across both VOICE and COMPETITOR rows but split 'University of Verona' from 'IT-SRC-OPENALEX' even though both are OpenAlex science). Join on sourceId only.

The source-detail cross-link depends on a collection owned by another domain. sources.id is demo-polluted for 6 of 31 rows. If the SOURCES owner does not expose a clean sourceId, the 'LATEST CAPTURES · N IN ARCHIVE' block will show 0 for those 6 sources and no one will notice.

18 rows carry the literal string 'NAO SEI' in the date field and 17 of them are VOICES (all 17 IG.VOICES.DATE are 'NAO SEI'). If any code path does new Date(a.date) or a string sort, these will land somewhere arbitrary. Handle dateState explicitly.

Line 3332's unguarded D.ARCHIVE.find(a => a.type === t).typeColor throws the moment a listed type has zero rows. A naive port that swaps D.ARCHIVE for the real collection while keeping the hardcoded 9-type list at line 3331 will crash the Archive view immediately, because 5 of those 9 types have zero real rows.

The title re-composition at line 3326 splits the title on ' · ' and translates each part through T.ARCHTYPES/T.CROPS/T.ISSUES. That was safe on generated titles. On real titles it is not — it would chop publisher headlines and scientific paper titles (e.g. the Xylella fastidiosa paper title) at arbitrary separators and risks truncating a taxonomic name, which §11 forbids. This code must be deleted, not adapted.
openQuestions: Should the 29 WINDOW rows (upstream PROVENANCE 'EXPECTED_NORM', no url, source literal 'CANONICAL') be in the archive at all? Excluding them gives a cleaner 711-row archive of genuinely captured artefacts — but then legacyCaseId and region drop to 0/711 and the 'VIEW IN ARCHIVE →' link from every opportunity detail must be removed rather than degraded.

Two of the 8 NEWS publishers do not resolve to a source-registry id because of name drift ('Agronotizie' vs 'AgroNotizie (Image Line)'; 'Consorzio Fitosanitario di Modena' vs 'Consorzio Fitosanitario Provinciale di Modena'). Should these be normalized upstream in the ingest, or left null? I did not fuzzy-match them — that is a guess, not a derivation.

The crop dimension has 47 distinct values across 5 incompatible vocabularies (canonical English, uppercase codes, Latin binomials, generic Italian words, olive-oil grades). Is normalizing them an upstream ingest job for the next package, or does the portal ship a visibly-grouped dropdown that admits the vocabularies are different?

Should COMPETITOR ad copy (IG.COMP_ACTIVITIES.text, 392/503) be shown verbatim in the drawer? It is public observed communication and §11 says do not translate it — but it is also marketing prose from a competitor rendered inside an ADAMA product, which may need a label rather than a design decision from me.

The 'CONNECTED TO' column loses its meaning once opportunity links cover only 3.9% of rows. Does the product owner want the column repurposed (source / company / kind-appropriate relation) or emptied and the grid narrowed? §12 says preserve component proportions, so I propose repurposing, but this is a product call.

modelChanges.why: There is no real people directory in the contract today. IG.PEOPLE is not exposed at all and IG.RESEARCHERS comes out empty-fielded. The Sources → People screen, the person detail, the search PEOPLE group and the 'People monitored' KPI all need ONE normalized list so the view can be dumb. Merging is required because 9 of the 15 IG.PEOPLE records are the same human as an IG.RESEARCHERS record under a differently-accented spelling (measured: Sattin, Scarabel, Panozzo, Loddo, Marzachì/Marzachi, Galetto, Angelini, Filippin, Bosco).
modelChanges.derivation: Union of IG.RESEARCHERS[60] and IG.PEOPLE[15], keyed on PERSON normalized with .normalize('NFD').replace(/[̀-ͯ]/g,'').toLowerCase(). 66 distinct records. Every string passes through UNK(v) = /^N[ÃA]O SEI/i.test(v) ? null : S(v) BEFORE anything else — 60/60 ROLE, 60/60 FACT_REGION and 6/60 ORCID carry that literal marker today.
fields: id — RESEARCHERS.ID (IT-PER-001..060) preferred on merge; PEOPLE.ID (IT-PER-061..075) otherwise. Keep alsoIds:[] for the merged pair so old links resolve.
name — PERSON verbatim, accents preserved, never translated (PRODUCT LAW §11).
category — CATEGORY. Measured union: RESEARCHER 62, INSTITUTIONAL_EXPERT 2, COMPANY_PERSON 1, CREATOR 1.

roleCat — presentation label mapped 1:1 from category: RESEARCHER→'RESEARCHERS', INSTITUTIONAL_EXPERT→'INSTITUTIONAL EXPERTS', CREATOR→'INFLUENCERS / CREATORS', COMPANY_PERSON→'COMPANY PEOPLE'. Emit ONLY categories that have ≥1 record.

role — UNK(PEOPLE.ROLE). Measured 5/15 non-null: 'coordenador do GIRE' (Sattin), 'membro do GIRE' (Loddo), 'responsavel do setor' (Boncompagni), 'Marketing Technical Manager' (Casagrandi, ADAMA Italia), 'formacao declarada em Scienze Agrarie...' (Castaldi). 61/66 → null. Needs IT/EN translation of these five, or show verbatim with a source note.
roleEvidence — PEOPLE.ROLE_EVIDENCE (15/15). Render next to role; the fixture's LAW field says it explicitly: knowing who someone is is not knowing what they do.

identityState — RESEARCHERS.IDENTITY_STATUS. Measured: ORCID_PRESENT_NOT_RESOLVED_HERE 54, NO_ORCID_IN_SOURCE 6. This REPLACES the demo's binary 'real identity' / 'demo profile' label, which is a claim the data does not support — an ORCID that was never resolved is not a confirmed identity.
institutions — RESEARCHERS.INSTITUTIONS (array, 60/60; lengths measured 1:31, 2:21, 3:8) or [PEOPLE.ORGANIZATION] (15/15). orgLabel = institutions.join(' · ').
affiliationCaveat — constant, from the source's own LIMITATIONS field (IT-SRC-OPENALEX): affiliation belongs to the AUTHOR, not to the study. Must be shown wherever an institution is shown.

orcid — RESEARCHERS.ORCID when it starts with 'https://orcid.org/' (54/60), else null. openalexId — RESEARCHERS.OPENALEX_ID (60/60 valid URLs). These two are the only real outbound links a person record has.

theme — RESEARCHERS.THEME code. Measured exactly 12 researchers per theme × 5 themes: VINE_FLAVESCENCE, DURUM_FUSARIUM, OLIVE_BACTROCERA, MAIZE_BORER_DIABROTICA, WEED_HERBICIDE_RESISTANCE. themeLabel from IG.THEMES by THEME.
worksInScope — RESEARCHERS.WORKS_IN_SCOPE (60/60, range 1..30, sum 383). This is works INSIDE the monitored query recorte, not a career total — the label must say so.

lastActivity — RESEARCHERS.LAST_ACTIVITY (60/60, real dates 2019-01-02..2026-07-30). daysFromRef via AM.daysFrom, never new Date(). Measured against REF 2026-09-02: only 19/60 within 12 months, 10/60 at 12-24 months, 31/60 older than 24 months.
factRegion — always null (60/60 carry the unknown marker). Expose as null so the view renders NON OSSERVABILE, never a region.
sourceId — 'IT-SRC-OPENALEX' 60/60 for researchers; PEOPLE records carry PROVENANCE REAL_SOURCE.
provenance — provOf(r, P.REAL_SOURCE) → REAL_SOURCE for all 66.

A theme is the scope of the OpenAlex QUERY, not a declared crop the person works on. Replace the two chip rows with ONE theme chip labelled 'tema monitorato', and do not silently re-badge it as a crop.

risks: The People screen gets visibly emptier and older. Today a card shows platform, region, crops, issues, a topic sentence, '3 opportunities · 3 signals' and a reassuring '16d ago'. After the migration it shows a name, institutions, one theme, a works count and a real LAST_ACTIVITY that for 31 of 60 people is more than two years old (measured against REF 2026-09-02: 19 within 12 months, 10 at 12-24 months, 31 older). That is the honest picture and PRODUCT LAW §3 says a smaller truthful screen wins — but it will be noticed, so say it out loud rather than letting it be discovered.

The person detail loses three of its five cards. Connected opportunities, connected signals and source history all go, and the header drops from three KPI tiles to two. There is a strong temptation to backfill with 'related by theme' opportunity links. Do not: the theme→crop→case chain is exactly the fabricated join being removed.

Count changes are user-visible in two places at once: People monitored 39 → 66 and Researchers 14 → 60. Both go UP, which reads as good news, but the underlying screen gets thinner. Do not let the rising count be used to justify keeping the thick card layout.

The theme→researcher join needs D.SCI_THEMES to map onto the five upstream THEME codes. If that map is written carelessly (for example by title-matching), a researcher can be attached to the wrong theme — recreating the exact class of invented edge being deleted. It should be an explicit, reviewed 5-row literal.

Nine people exist twice (once in IG.RESEARCHERS, once in IG.PEOPLE) under differently-accented spellings, and one of them, Maurizio Sattin, appears as IT-PER-051 and IT-PER-061. A naive union yields 75 records and inflates every count by 9. The accent-folded merge must be tested explicitly.

Six researchers carry the literal 'NÃO SEI' in the ORCID field itself. Building an href from that value produces a link to https://orcid.org/NÃO SEI. Guard on the 'https://orcid.org/' prefix, not on truthiness.

The list is not all Italian. Measured affiliations include All-Russian Institute of Plant Protection (2) and a German viticulture institute (3). Any heading or export that calls these 'Italian researchers' is a new factual error introduced by the migration itself.

LAST_ACTIVITY is the date of the last work indexed inside the monitored query recorte. If it is rendered with the existing ago() relative formatter next to a person's name it will read as 'we last saw this person N days ago', which is a field-observation claim. Render an absolute date with an explicit label.

Removing D.TSR from the People directory breaks two existing deep links (portale.html:3114 and goTsr at 3404) that navigate to sourceGroup PEOPLE with peopleCat TECHNICAL SALES REPRESENTATIVES. Both land on an empty filtered screen if only the data is changed and the routes are left behind.

The 8 competitor 'PEOPLE mention' activities call openPerson with demo P-* ids (measured 8/8 resolving today). They are another domain's records but they break in this domain's view; without coordination the person route will throw or fall back to people[0], silently showing the wrong human.

IG.PEOPLE.ROLE and ROLE_EVIDENCE are written in Portuguese ('coordenador do GIRE', 'duas rotas independentes: video publico e indice bibliografico'). Shipping them verbatim into an Italian-default UI is wrong; machine-translating a provenance statement is also wrong. This needs a decision, not a default.
openQuestions: D.SCI_THEMES has no upstream THEME code. Should the 5-row map (grapevine-phytoplasma → VINE_FLAVESCENCE, etc.) be written in the view, or should the Science-domain owner add the code to the theme record so both domains read one key? These two domains collide here; whoever goes second must not write a second map.

IG.PEOPLE.ROLE carries five real Portuguese role strings and IDENTITY_EVIDENCE / ROLE_EVIDENCE are whole Portuguese sentences. Translate to IT/EN, show verbatim with a 'source note' label, or omit until the upstream pack supplies IT? PRODUCT LAW §11 protects names and original public quotes, but these are Sintonia's own annotations, not quotes.

Mirco Casagrandi is a real ADAMA Italia employee (Marketing Technical Manager) present as a REAL_SOURCE record with public evidence. Should ADAMA's own people appear in an external-intelligence directory at all, and if so under which category label? He is currently the only COMPANY_PERSON.

Does the person detail survive as a route at all for the 61 people who have no publications, no region, no role and no observation history — or should the directory card simply not be clickable for them? A detail page with two facts on it may be worse than no detail page.

Should the two non-Italian-affiliated clusters (All-Russian Institute of Plant Protection, Weinsberg) be filtered out of the researcher list, or kept with the honest 'monitored theme, not Italian scope' framing? Filtering changes 60 into a smaller number that no upstream field justifies.

IG.THEMES carries AUTHORS_IT (334, 235, 223, 62, 22 — total 876) while only 60 researchers were ingested. Should the Science screen state that 60 is a top-N slice of a much larger author population? Showing 60 without that denominator invites reading it as the whole field.

domain: SCIENTIFIC INTELLIGENCE (themes, research records, institutions, researchers, resistance)
summary: Today the Science screen shows 13 "classified themes" (10 from D.SCI_THEMES + 3 from ITALY_SCIENCE.EXTRA_THEMES), a 36-row "RECENT RESEARCH" table, a 14-name "RESEARCHERS" panel, a 12-row "INSTITUTIONS · 12" panel, a GIRE resistance block, and a per-theme detail view (isTheme, markup 2157-2184). Only two of those blocks stand on real ingested data: the GIRE resistance block (portale.html 3244-3300 reads window.ITALY_INGEST.RESISTANCE directly, 34 cases, every field 34/34 populated) and 12 of the 36 research rows (which come from window.ITALY_REAL.SCIENCE, an older hand-curated fixture, not from IG). The other 24 research rows are procedurally generated in italy-demo-data.js:385-389 with seed() — fabricated year, institution, study type, descriptor, "why" prose and study location. The 12 institutions are a hardcoded name array (italy-demo-data.js:370) whose record counts are counted over those fabricated rows. The real backing is IG.THEMES (5), IG.SCIENCE (88), IG.RESEARCHERS (60) and IG.RESISTANCE (34); italy-app-model.js already exposes scienceRecords/researchers/resistance but three of its science field mappings are dead (measured 0/88 and 0/60) because it reads demo-era key names that the real schema does not have.
realSource: APP.collections.scienceRecords (88, from IG.SCIENCE) + APP.collections.researchers (60, from IG.RESEARCHERS) + APP.collections.resistance (34, from IG.RESISTANCE) + a NEW APP.collections.scienceThemes projected from IG.THEMES (5). Institutions must be DERIVED, and there are two distinct and non-interchangeable derivations: (a) IG.SCIENCE[].INSTITUTION — 6 distinct values, the FIRST AUTHOR's affiliation on each of the 88 records: University of Verona 27, University of Turin 25, University of Milan 16, Institute of Sciences of Food Production 15, INRAE 3, Instituto de Agricultura Sostenible 2 (the last two are French and Spanish, not Italian); (b) IG.THEMES[].INSTITUTIONS_TOP — 37 distinct institutions with a per-theme WORKS count (11-12 per theme). (a) counts records in this corpus; (b) counts works in the upstream OpenAlex theme query. They must never be summed or shown under one label. window.ITALY_SCIENCE stays as an explicitly-labelled interpretation layer, but only for the 5 theme keys that have a real counterpart.

risks: The screen gets visibly emptier and the numbers get visibly smaller: 13 themes -> 5, 12 institutions -> 6, 36 'records' -> 88 (this one grows), 14 researchers -> 60. Three of the five theme detail pages will have an empty publications list. Someone will read that as a regression. It is not; it is the first honest version of this screen.

The 88-record corpus is 7 authors deep. If the count ships without that caption next to it, it will be quoted as 'Sintonia monitors 88 Italian studies' and there is no way to walk that back later. This is the highest-consequence item in the whole domain.

Two of the six real institutions are not Italian (INRAE, France; Instituto de Agricultura Sostenible, Spain). Any header wording like 'Italian institutions' becomes false the moment the panel is repointed.

IG.SCIENCE has no theme key. The record<->theme join is inferred from CROP+ISSUE and it leaves 5 of 88 records (IT-SCI-001, 002, 086, 087, 088) belonging to no theme. Those records must stay reachable in the flat table, or 5 real records silently vanish from the product.

INSTITUTION on a record is the FIRST author's affiliation, and INSTITUTIONS_TOP on a theme is a works count from a different query. The two panels sit within 20 lines of each other in the markup (2082 and 2175) and mixing their denominators is the easiest mistake available here.

IG.RESEARCHERS.ROLE and FACT_REGION are 60/60 Portuguese analyst notes ('NÃO SEI — ...'). They already flow through the app model unfiltered. Any view that binds AM researcher role today ships that note to the user; the guard must land in the model, not in one view.

The theme<->opportunity link is deleted in three places (case detail 2628, archive detail 3340, theme detail 2176). If any of the three is missed, a fixture-only relationship keeps rendering while the other two disappear, which is worse than either state alone.

T.CROPS / T.ISSUES do not have entries for a single real token. Repointing the view without the token->label map first will put VINE, DURUM_WHEAT and FLAVESCENCE on an Italian screen in raw uppercase.

th0 falls back to sciDetailThemes[0]. Every existing link and bookmark to a demo theme id (8 of 10 ids disappear) will silently render a different theme's facts under the requested id unless STEP 13 lands with STEP 8.

winFor2() (line 3197) reads D.WINDOWS and turns it into 'WINDOW OPEN · N days remaining'. It belongs to the windows domain but is invoked from buildTheme, so it can be missed by both owners. Coordinate this one line explicitly.

ITALY_SCIENCE.B is authored interpretation, not a fixture, and the UI already labels it honestly. Deleting it wholesale would remove the one thing on the screen that connects science to business. Deleting only the 5 orphan keys is the right cut, and it is a judgement call worth confirming with the product owner.
openQuestions: ITALY_SCIENCE.B is Sintonia's own business interpretation, already labelled on screen as 'an interpretation layer over the science, not a scientific conclusion'. Does Rule 2 (a demo fixture may never supply a fact) apply to it? My reading: the rel/short/why/shows/notShows prose is interpretation, allowed, but ONLY over a theme that really exists upstream — so keep the 5 mapped keys, drop the 5 orphans. Confirm before deleting authored copy.

The three EXTRA_THEMES (herbicide resistance, weed management, biocontrol) declare works:null and 'not ingested' in their own text. Should they stay visible under a separate labelled heading (my recommendation, since they document a known gap), or be removed until data exists?

IG.THEMES.WORKS (135/70/71/27/17) counts works matching an OpenAlex QUERY. IG.SCIENCE holds 88 harvested records. These are two different universes and the theme detail page will show both at once (works 71, records 0 for OLIVE_BACTROCERA). What exact wording distinguishes them on screen?
Is there an upstream plan to add a THEME key to IG.SCIENCE? If yes, the CROP+ISSUE join in STEP 4 is temporary scaffolding and should be marked as such in a comment.
The 'BUSINESS RELEVANCE' column of the records table (SB.RECORD_REL, keyed by demo themeId) can only resolve for the two themes that have records. Keep the column with blanks, or drop the column?

Does any other domain already bind AM.collections.researchers[].role or .org? If so the Portuguese note may already be on screen somewhere I did not look, and the model-side guard becomes urgent rather than tidy.

window.ITALY_REAL.SCIENCE (12) and .RESEARCHERS (14) are an earlier hand-curated real fixture with fields IG does not have (kind, what, region, focus, note). Is it superseded by IG entirely, or is it a second real source that should be merged? I assumed superseded; it is the one assumption in this spec I could not settle from the data alone.

fields: id — s.ID (stable upstream key; replaces the demo SRC-nn id for the 6 name-colliding records)
sourceId — s.SOURCE_ID || s.ID (SOURCE_ID present on only 11/31; ID is the primary key)

type — S(s.TYPE) [31/31; 12 distinct values: OFFICIAL 5, FIELD 6, TECHNICAL_MEDIA 4, COMPETITOR 4, COOPERATIVE 3, RESEARCH 2, RESEARCH_INSTITUTION 2, MARKET 1, COMPANY 1, PEOPLE 1, PRODUCER_ORG 1, ADAMA 1]
role — S(s.ROLE) [27/31 non-empty, 1 of those is the literal 'NÃO SEI' → 26/31 informative]; replaces the demo 'what' column

frequency — S(s.FREQUENCY) [27/31 non-null, but 13 are the crawler token 'DATED' and 3 'NO_DATE_FOUND' → only 11/31 carry a human cadence]

The registry drops 53→31 rows, the source-detail page loses three of its five cards, the news feed loses its period filter and four card fields, the UPCOMING EVENTS rail drops 5→2, and the competitor participation table disappears. PRODUCT LAW §3 says a smaller truthful screen beats a dense fake one, but someone will read this as regression — the counts above should ship WITH the change.

The 'RECORD COLLEGATI' column will be 0 for 23 of 31 sources. That is the honest state (two thirds of the registry is a listening list that has not yet fed a record), but a column of zeros invites someone to 'fix' it by re-deriving from names or topics. It must not be.

domain: NAV COUNTERS + DATA STATE / PROVENANCE PANEL + NOTIFICATIONS
summary: Today the chrome of the portal — left nav counts, the sidebar "today" box, the 8 radar KPI cards, the 20-tile region map, the 7 source tiles, the transparency ("DEMO ENVIRONMENT") panel and the notification bell — is almost entirely fed by one object, `D.KPI` (aliased `K` at portale.html:2549), plus `D.WINDOW_KPI`, `D.FIELD_KPI`, `D.REGION_STATS`, `D.WHAT_CHANGED` and `D.NOTIFICATIONS`. Those are computed inside italy-demo-data.js from the demo fixtures (29 demo CASES, 72 demo ACTIVITIES, 56 demo SIGNALS, 53 demo SOURCES, 448-row demo ARCHIVE, 36 demo RECORDS, 39 demo PEOPLE), so every badge is a fixture number even when a real one exists. Measured, the gap is large and always in the same direction: competitors nav says 72, real is 503; science says 36, real is 88; archive says 448, real is 740; sources says 92, real is 31; "competitor movements · 30d" says 43, real is 11; the transparency panel claims 244 real / 491 demo when the real application model holds 1038 real / 100 demo records. Four numbers are honest by luck (29 windows, 6 window-open, 2 next-cycle, 5 date-unknown) because the demo CASES are a 1:1 shadow of the 29 canonical windows. The transparency panel itself is the worst offender in principle: it is the screen that promises to tell the truth about the data, and it reads the fixture (`D.ACTIVITIES`, `D.ARCHIVE`, `D.FIELD_MESSAGES`) to do it. `D.NOTIFICATIONS` is six hand-written alerts asserting field messages, window countdowns and a BASF movement that exist nowhere in the ingested data.
realSource: APP = window.ITALY_APP_MODEL. Nav and KPI counts come from APP.counts / APP.collections (windows 29 · competitorActivities 503 · scienceRecords 88 · archive 740 · sources 31 · researchers 60 · voices 17 · products 166 · marketObservations 77 · resistance 34 · channels 30 · events 18 · news 8 · futureSignals 3 · upstreamOpportunities 3). Verified portfolio matches come from window.ITALY_LABEL_VERDICTS (VERIFIED 12 / NOT_FOUND 7) — which italy-app-model.js does NOT read yet. Regulatory use rows come from IG.LINKS (219). Source-group tiles come from IG.SOURCES[].TYPE (31 records). The transparency panel comes from APP.provenanceSummary. fields: cropKey — mapped from GROUP + PRODUCT with an explicit, declared lookup: GROUP 'OLIVE_OIL' -> 'Olive'; GROUP 'WINE' -> 'Grapevine'; PRODUCT 'MAI|FEED' or 'Feed maize' -> 'Maize'; 'BLTPAN|PAN' or 'Breadmaking common wheat' -> 'Wheat'; 'DUR|UNKNOWN' or 'Durum wheat' -> 'Durum Wheat'; 'ORGFOUR|FEED' or 'Feed barley' -> 'Barley'. One record has PRODUCT null (IT-MKT-077, the wine row) and must resolve by GROUP only. Anything unmatched stays null and is never silently attached to a crop.
periodStart / periodEnd — ISO dates parsed from REFERENCE_PERIOD, which is always 'dd/mm/yyyy..dd/mm/yyyy' (present on 77/77)
daysSinceObservation — AM.daysFrom(periodEnd), so no view calls new Date()

hasStage — STAGE non-null on only 40/77; the four observed values are 'Price at farm gate' (11), 'Deliver to first customer - silo or processing plant - on truck or other transport means' (13), 'Departure from farm or from production area - on truck or other transport means' (12), 'National Average - Not Specified' (4). Rows with different stages must never be averaged.

risks: The screen shrinks hard. Of roughly 14 rendered components on the crop tab, 9 disappear outright and 2 more lose their headline number. Rule 3 says a smaller truthful screen wins and rule 12 says do not redesign, so the engineer must resist the instinct to backfill the empty grid space.

Blast radius outside the domain. The temperature verdict is read on five other screens (Radar 679, Crop Windows 732/2762, Competitor Watch 1693, Science 2132, Opportunity case 329-336). Removing it silently changes four other people's screens. This must be sequenced with them, not done unilaterally.

The crop mapping is an interpretation, not a field. 'MAI|FEED', 'BLTPAN|PAN', 'DUR|UNKNOWN', 'ORGFOUR|FEED' are EC product codes; nothing upstream says MAI = Maize. It is a safe reading, but it must be declared in the model and visible on screen, and 'DUR|UNKNOWN' carries an explicit unknown quality class that must not be presented as 'durum fino'.

Stale data can be read as current. 12 of 77 rows are on stopped series and their own SERIES_WARNING says the last quotation is NOT a current price — including the only Grapevine row (stopped 2025) and 10 of the 36 olive rows (some last quoted in 2010). If the piazza table renders them plainly, the screen becomes less trustworthy than the fixture it replaced.

Unit and stage collisions. Olive is EUR/100kg, cereals EUR/t, wine Euro/HL; and 40 of 77 rows carry a STAGE (farm gate vs delivery to first customer vs departure from farm) while 37 carry none. Any averaging, ranking or single 'the price' headline across those is methodologically wrong.

One source, one point in time. All 77 rows come from a single provider (EC Agri-food Data Portal) and only the latest observation of each series was ingested, though the source holds 190-364 points per series. The screen must not imply a monitored multi-source market picture.

Numbers the business already saw will change downward. The ADAMA panel's product count drops for 5 of 8 crops (Maize 11->3, Durum 9->3, Grapevine 8->1) and the opportunities count drops from 29 to 3 application-wide. Someone will read that as a regression rather than a correction; it needs to be announced, not just shipped.

Three crop tabs go empty and one uncovered crop (Barley, 8 real observations) has no home. Whatever is decided, the nav badge, the crop rail and the sc-for placeholder hints must be updated together or the rail will render ghosts.

MK.INTERNAL is currently unreachable, so deleting it is invisible in QA. If only the cpMarketObj prop is removed and the constant is left in italy-market-pulse.js, the next person to build an 'internal data' card will find it sitting there ready to use.
openQuestions: IG.MARKET_SUMMARIES points at five written analyses (MAIS, FRUMENTO DURO, OLIVO/OLIO DI OLIVA, VITE/VINO, RISO — 22k to 33k characters each) whose .md bodies are not in the client bundle. Is that upstream prose the intended replacement for the fixture reading/commentary, and should it be ingested? If yes, most of what I marked REMOVE could come back with provenance.

Rice has an upstream market summary and a canonical window but zero price observations and no crop tab. Barley has 8 current price observations and no tab, no window, no summary. What decides which crops get a Market Pulse tab — portfolio relevance, window coverage, or data coverage?

Should the FEASIBILITY audit table survive? It is methodology rather than fact, which makes it legal, but every row currently names a route (ISMEA, CUN, BMTI, Eurostat, JRC MARS) that was never connected, so as printed it overstates what the product can do today.

The EC records give week-on-week and year-on-year percentages per piazza (72/77 and 67/77 present). Is showing those percentages acceptable, or does a per-piazza percentage read as a market trend and therefore fall under the rule against presentation inventing a state?

Who owns the removal of the market temperature from the four other screens, and does the Crop Windows drawer keep its 'MARKET PULSE ... context, not proof of demand' box at all once there is no verdict to put in it?

The i18n key t.cannotProveList and t.notObservableNote are correct and should stay, but t.subMarket still promises 'condizioni, dinamica, offerta, fiducia e prospettive' — dynamics, supply, confidence and outlook all die in this migration. Who rewrites that subtitle in both languages?

summary: Today the whole Competitor Watch screen is fed by window.ITALY_DEMO: 72 fabricated activities across 6 companies and 6 activity types (PAID 23, ORGANIC 16, VIDEO 10, PEOPLE 8, EVENT 9, PRODUCT/PORTFOLIO 6), plus 4 pre-baked demo aggregates (D.MATRIX, D.CROP_COLS, D.ISSUE_ROWS, D.WHAT_CHANGED) and 14 fabricated competitor products (D.CPRODUCTS). modelChanges.collection: competitorActivities (extend the existing projection, italy-app-model.js lines 132-148)
modelChanges.why: The view currently reads scalar a.crop / a.issue / a.product / a.days that do not exist, and re-derives crop names by string equality against demo crop labels. Normalizing once in the model keeps the view dumb and stops each widget inventing its own crop match.
fields: cropsCanonical: string[] — resolved ONLY through an explicit botanical/common-name identity table (Vitis vinifera->Grapevine, Zea mays->Maize, Olea europaea->Olive, Solanum lycopersicum->Tomato, Malus domestica->Apple, Triticum aestivum->Wheat, Oryza sativa->Rice, Beta vulgaris->Sugar Beet, Helianthus annuus->Sunflower, Prunus persica->Peach, Citrus->Citrus). This is a taxonomic identity, not an interpretation. Measured: 132/503 activities resolve to at least one canonical crop.

cropScope: 'RESOLVED' | 'GENERIC_TERM' | 'NOT_OBSERVED' — GENERIC_TERM for the advertiser's own umbrella words (colture 59, cereali 24, frutta 8, ortaggi 5; 51 activities carry only such a term), NOT_OBSERVED for the 320 activities with an empty crops array. A generic term is never promoted to a crop.
issuesObserved: string[] = a.issues verbatim (98/503 non-empty; 14 distinct terms, mixed Italian generic and Latin binomial). Never translated, never truncated at '(' per §11.
issueScope: 'SPECIES' | 'GENERIC_TERM' | 'NOT_OBSERVED' — SPECIES only when the term is a capitalised binomial. Measured: 30/503 activities carry a species-level issue.

hasDate: boolean (414 true / 89 false) and dateState: 'OBSERVED' | 'NOT_OBSERVED'. Every widget that sorts or buckets by time must read hasDate and put the 89 undated records in an explicit 'DATA NON OSSERVATA' bucket rather than at day 0.

displayName: string = page || company — the observed Facebook page name ('Bayer Crop Science Italia', 414/503) is a real field and replaces the fabricated companyLabel. When page is null the card shows the company name plus 'CANALE NON RISOLTO'.

textExcerpt: string|null = text verbatim (392/503, average 239 characters). It is the advertiser's own public copy and replaces the fabricated headline. It is displayed as a quoted excerpt and is NEVER parsed to extract a crop, issue, product or claim.

relatedWindows: {windowId, crop, issue, region, status, startDate}[] — populated only when cropsCanonical intersects a canonical window's CROP_NAME AND the activity carries a SPECIES-level issue that equals the window's ISSUE_NAME under an upstream-supplied synonym table. Empty otherwise; the model must not fall back to crop-only matching, because a shared crop name is not a relationship.

geoLabel: 'RAGGIUNTO IN ITALIA' for the 414 REACHED_IN_ITALY, 'MULTIPAESE / NON RISOLTO' for the 89. geoCaveat: the verbatim countrySem string 'AD_REACHED_COUNTRY != AD_TARGETED_COUNTRY' must be shown on the paid card so reach is never read as targeting.

modelChanges.why: The view builds companies from a 6-row fixture with invented counts, themes and confidence. IG.COMP_COMPANIES cannot be used raw because it has 14 rows for 11 companies — the paid rows are title-case (Bayer, IT-COMP-004, 69 paid) and the organic rows are upper-case (BAYER, IT-COMP-010, 17 organic). Merging must happen once, in the model.
fields: company: string — canonical title-case name taken from COMP_ACTIVITIES.company (11 distinct: BASF, FMC, Corteva, Bayer, Syngenta, UPL, Sipcam, Certis, Sumitomo, Gowan, Nufarm)
paidAdsReachingIt: number (sum of PAID_ADS_REACHING_IT across the merged rows)
observedTotal: number — verified to equal paid+organic per company (BASF 138, FMC 102, Corteva 94, Bayer 86, Syngenta 55, UPL 13, Sipcam 6, Certis 4, Sumitomo 2, Gowan 2, Nufarm 1; total 503)
pages: string[] (union of PAGES; empty for the 5 organic-only companies)

products: reference into competitorProducts (measured: Bayer has 0 proven products despite 86 activities — that must render as 'NESSUN PRODOTTO PROVATO NELLA LETTURA ATTUALE', never as an empty list with no note)
firstObserved / lastObserved: ISO date|null — null for Sipcam, Certis, Sumitomo, Nufarm, Gowan (no dated record). Must render 'DATA NON OSSERVATA'.
observedLast30: number — feeds the 'new' counter on the company strip; the 7-day counter is not viable (measured 1 record in 7 days)
activeAds: number — count of active === 'ACTIVE' (measured: FMC 17, Corteva 5, Bayer 5, all others 0; 27 total, plus 2 NOT_KNOWN)

Not measurable. No real issue term carries a case id.
There is no field linking a company to a case or an opportunity. A shared crop is not a relationship.

risks: The screen gets visibly emptier per card while the totals get much bigger (72 -> 503). A reader who only looks at the header will think the product improved; a reader who opens a card will think it regressed. The what-changed strip in particular goes from six confident tiles to essentially one number, because only 1 real record falls inside 7 days.

320 of 503 activities carry no crop and 405 carry no issue. Any widget that groups by crop or issue silently describes a minority of the corpus. Every such panel must publish its own denominator or it will be read as covering everything.

The botanical-to-common-name mapping (Vitis vinifera -> Grapevine) is safe, but the temptation to extend it to the umbrella words (colture, cereali, frutta, ortaggi — 96 activities) is not. 'cereali' is the advertiser's word for an unspecified set; turning it into Wheat would manufacture a fact.

Latin binomials are both crop names and issue names in this corpus, and §11 forbids translating them or truncating at '('. A generic il()/cl() translation pass over the issue filter would corrupt 'Plasmopara viticola' into a Sintonia label.

The 89 ORGANIC_VIDEO records are near-empty (no date, url, text, country, crop, issue). They are real and must be counted, but any list that sorts or filters by time will drop them without saying so. If they are quietly excluded, the company totals on two different panels will disagree (e.g. Syngenta 55 total but 30 in any dated view).

REACHED_IN_ITALY is already correct in the model, but the countrySem string literally says AD_REACHED_COUNTRY != AD_TARGETED_COUNTRY. If the card shows only the flag and drops the caveat, 414 reach observations silently become 414 Italian targeting claims.

IG.COMP_COMPANIES' case-duplicate rows (Bayer/BAYER, Corteva/CORTEVA, Syngenta/SYNGENTA) will double-count company totals if merged naively by exact string. Bayer would show 69 paid on one panel and 86 total on another.

The ADAMA-portfolio side of this domain currently rests entirely on D.CASES[].productLinks, which italy-app-model.js reads at lines 102-105 while never reading ITALY_LABEL_VERDICTS. Until step 5 lands, any 'portfolio' wording anywhere in Competitor Watch is demo-backed. This is a cross-domain dependency and the serial engineer should not let a competitor-side edit ship a portfolio claim ahead of it.

The matrix and issue-table markup hard-code their column counts in grid-template-columns strings that appear twice each (header row and data row). Changing one and not the other misaligns the table without any error.
openQuestions: Can upstream supply a synonym table mapping observed advertiser issue terms to canonical ISSUE_NAMEs (Plasmopara viticola -> Downy Mildew, Erysiphe necator -> Powdery Mildew, Zymoseptoria tritici -> Septoria Leaf Blotch, Ceratitis capitata -> Mediterranean Fruit Fly)? Without it the COMPETITOR x ISSUE table can show no portfolio column and the Competitor x Window cross-link resolves for almost nothing (only 30 of 503 activities carry a species-level issue at all).

Should Citrus, Sunflower and Peach appear in the crop density and matrix even though they have no canonical crop window? They are real observed communication (15, 9 and 2 items) but they cannot cross-link to anything. My recommendation is yes, with no window column.

What is the actual collection horizon of the Meta Ad Library pull? The corpus spans 2019-12-05 to 2026-08-26 but per-company first dates differ wildly (BASF 2023-03, FMC 2025-10). If the horizon is per-page rather than global, even the per-company 'first observed' date is not comparable across companies and should be suppressed, not just the lead-time card.

The reference date is 2026-09-02 and the latest observation is 2026-08-26. Is the corpus a one-off load or will it refresh? If it will not refresh, every 'last 30 days' widget on this screen will decay into an empty box and should be reframed as a fixed observation period with explicit start and end dates.

Do the 89 ORGANIC_VIDEO records have any recoverable metadata upstream (title, publish date, url, view count)? IG.CHANNELS carries EXAMPLE_TITLE / EXAMPLE_URL / VIEWS / EXAMPLE_PUBLISHED_AT for 30 channels — if those channels are the same YouTube sources, upstream may be able to attach dates and titles, which would restore the organic half of the feed. Until then the organic records are countable but not displayable as feed items.

Is the CREATIVE GALLERY worth keeping at all with no captured assets, or should the tab be removed so the remaining views (feed, by issue) are not diluted? This is a product decision, not an engineering one.

risks: The screen loses roughly 70% of its content. Measured honestly: the radar goes from 29 cards to 3, and the detail page loses the evidence bars, the competitor panel, the action map, the executive timeline, the field inbox, the adjacency map shading, the latin name, the origin tile and the label-timing line. What remains — title, what is happening with a named document and date, why it matters, what we know, what we do not know, interpretations, sources — is genuinely strong content, but it is one column where there were three. The client must be told BEFORE the edit, not after, and §3 forbids redesigning the screen to fill the hole.

The three real records are written in PORTUGUESE, and §11 makes Italian the default language. TITLE, CROP, ISSUE, CURRENT_EVIDENCE, WHAT_WE_KNOW, WHAT_WE_DO_NOT_KNOW and INTERPRETATIONS are all pt-BR ('Videira', 'Milho grao', 'a obrigacao de tratar o vetor e norma, nao recomendacao'). The regulatory quotes inside them are Italian. This is not a translation the engineer may perform — translating a source record is exactly the fact-mutation the product law forbids, and product/company/Latin names must not be touched at all. Either upstream reissues the records in Italian, or the portal ships with visibly Portuguese body text on its three real cards. Flag to the data owner before STEP 2.

ISSUE_TYPE on opp 003 is the literal string 'NAO SEI' ('I do not know'). The same literal appears across the real data: VOICES.REGION is 'NAO SEI' 17/17, NEWS.REGION 8/8, FUTURE_SIGNALS.REGION 2/3. Any code path that renders a raw field will print 'NAO SEI' to an Italian user. Every new binding needs an explicit guard mapping it to t.notKnown.

Four incompatible crop vocabularies coexist in the real data and the synonym table is load-bearing. Measured: OPPORTUNITIES.CROP is Portuguese; CANONICAL.CROP_NAME and D.CASES.crop are English; COMP_ACTIVITIES.crops is Latin/Italian ('Vitis vinifera' 42, 'Zea mays' 67, 'colture' 59, 'cereali' 24); VOICES.CROP and SCIENCE.CROP are SCREAMING_SNAKE ('VINE' 45, 'MAIZE' 8, 'DURUM_WHEAT' 40). If the table is wrong the detail page will show competitor and science cross-links belonging to the wrong crop — a silent wrong answer, worse than an empty panel. Build it as one reviewed literal and default to empty, never to a fuzzy match.

There is a FIFTH id space for cases. VOICES.CASE_ID measures as IT-VINE-FLAVESCENCE (8 voices), IT-MAIZE-WEED (8) and IT-DURUM_WHEAT-FUSARIUM (1). Only the first corresponds to a real opportunity. So if the detail page adds a field-voices panel, opp 001 gets 8 voices and opp 002 and 003 get zero — and the 8 MAIZE voices are about WEEDS, not the piralide that opp 002 is about. Do not join maize to maize.

All 29 canonical windows measure PROVENANCE = 'EXPECTED_NORM', SOURCE_IDS = [] and PRODUCT_MATCHES = []. They are audited agronomic norms, not observations, and they carry no traceable source. Treating them as the radar's real feed instead of the 3 opportunities would produce a denser and more comfortable screen that still cannot answer 'who published this'. That temptation will present itself around STEP 9 when the KPI numbers look thin. Windows already have their own screen; leave them there.

MARKET_CONTEXT, COMPETITOR_CONTEXT and FIELD_VOICES are present on 3/3 records but their values are folder paths ('ver 01-DESIGN-READY/MARKET-PULSE/'). They look like fields and are not data. Any engineer scanning the schema will try to render them. They must be dropped in the mapper, not passed through.

WHAT_IS_HAPPENING.SOURCE_ID is present 3/3 and resolvable 0/3 ('IT-T3-002', 'IT-T3-006 (ERSA FVG)', 'IT-T4-001' against an IG.SOURCES id set that only contains IT-SRC-* ids). Rendering it as a clickable source would produce dead links on every real card. Text only.
CURRENT_EVIDENCE and WHAT_WE_KNOW are byte-identical on all 3 records. Rendering both fills two panels with the same list and manufactures an appearance of corroboration. Render one.

decorate() at portale.html:2425 does `Object.assign(c, ...)` — it mutates its input. Because it is called per render (see the comment at 2516) it currently writes presentation labels back into the demo records. Reusing that pattern on AM.collections.opportunities.records would corrupt the shared model across views. decorateOpportunity must return a new object; this is easy to miss when copying the existing method.

Their D.CASES reads must be removed for this domain to be clean, so the serial engineer has to sequence these with the other domain owners or the same lines will be edited twice.

That affects the nav item, the i18n keys, the KPI tile and the page title — a naming decision, not an engineering one.

Is a canonical window allowed to be bound to a real opportunity by content match (crop + region + issue), given that LEGACY_CASE_ID does not connect the two id spaces? A content match is a judgement, and §7 says presentation may not invent an agronomic state. Recommendation: bind only opp 001 -> IT-WIN-0001 if a human confirms it, and leave the other two unbound.

Does the '29 canonical windows' number get to keep the word 'cases' anywhere in the UI, or must every occurrence be relabelled? The region map, the KPI status tiles and the windows nav badge all currently count windows while saying or implying cases.

modelChanges.why: The view must stop deriving status, dates and product links itself. Every field here is a direct copy or a rule-7-legal date arithmetic, so the calendar and the detail screen become dumb renderers.
fields: canonicalStatus — alias of status; exists purely to kill the portale.html:3004 defect where w.canonicalStatus is undefined and every product-page window reads DATE TO CONFIRM. Derivation: w.CURRENT_STATUS, 29/29 present.
open — status === 'WINDOW_OPEN'. Upstream decision only, never a date comparison. Measured 6/29 true.
hasDates — !!(START_DATE && END_DATE). Measured 24/29 true; the 5 false rows must render DATA DA CONFERMARE everywhere instead of a bar.
windowLabel — hasDates ? fmt(startDate) + ' -> ' + fmt(endDate) : null. Pure formatting of CANONICAL START_DATE/END_DATE.

observedStage / observedStageSource — from the joined IG.CROP_WINDOWS row's OBSERVED_STAGE, but ONLY when the string does not begin with 'NAO SEI' and does not contain 'nenhum boletim'. Measured: 5 of the 7 IG rows are explicit NAO SEI, and neither of the 2 real ones (Modena) matches a canonical region, so this is null 29/29 today. It exists so that the next data load lights the field up without a view change.

verifiedProducts — array of product names from ITALY_LABEL_VERDICTS.VERIFIED where tuple[0] === crop and normalizeIssue(tuple[1]) === normalizeIssue(issue). normalizeIssue must fold ' / ' and ' · ' to a single separator, otherwise IT-WIN-0016 'Cereal Aphids · BYDV Risk' misses the verdict 'Cereal Aphids / BYDV Risk'. Measured with folding: 12 tuples covering 11 of 29 windows; without folding, 10 windows.

labelVerdictState — 'VERIFIED_LABEL_MATCH' when verifiedProducts.length, else 'NO_CONFIRMED_MATCH_CURRENT_READING'. Rule 10: the UI string for the second value must be 'nessuna corrispondenza confermata nella lettura attuale', never 'ADAMA has no product'.

regulatory — the joined IG.CROP_WINDOWS record, matched on normalized crop (VITE->Grapevine, OLIVO->Olive) plus exact REGION. Measured join: 2 of 29 canonical windows (IT-WIN-0001 Veneto and IT-WIN-0008 Piemonte, both Flavescenza Dorata). Fields carried through: act (REGULATORY_ACT), actState (REGULATORY_ACT_STATE), regulatoryWindow, monitoringWindow, applicationWindow2026, nextImportantWindow, preparationWindow, coverageState, sourceId. null for the other 27.

risks: The screen gets visibly emptier and there is no way around it. The timeline loses the crop-cycle band, the weed band and the observed dot on every row; the region column loses its hectare line and its scale chip; the row count drops 40 -> 29; the season view loses its phase cards. What remains per row is: the canonical window bar, the preparation bar (labelled interpretation), a status chip, a date range and a product line. Rule 3 says a smaller truthful screen beats a dense fake one and rule 12 says do not redesign to compensate — the serial engineer must be told this is expected, not a bug, or the instinct will be to backfill.

Whole crops disappear from the crop rail. Wheat loses all five of its regions (no canonical Septoria window exists for Veneto, Piemonte, Lombardia, Toscana or Umbria) and Durum Wheat keeps 3 of 6. Anyone who has demoed the Wheat calendar will read this as a regression.

IG.CROP_WINDOWS free text is in Portuguese, not Italian — 'aberta — inicio de agosto a fim de setembro', 'FECHADA — as janelas obrigatorias terminaram em junho'. Piping it straight into an Italian-default UI (rule 11) would be worse than showing nothing. Either fence it as a verbatim analyst note or hold it back until the next ingest translates it.

The label-verdict join is separator-sensitive. IT-WIN-0016 'Cereal Aphids · BYDV Risk' versus the audit's 'Cereal Aphids / BYDV Risk' is the only case today, but the same class of mismatch will silently drop future matches. Normalize once in the model and never in a view.

strengthFor() and productByKey links in italy-app-model.js still route through D.CASES.productLinks (line 102). This domain does not own that path, but the window screens consume its output through wd.c.productObjs. If the products domain migrates on a different schedule, the window detail will briefly read verified products from one source and the case-derived list from another. Coordinate step 10 with whoever owns the products domain.

The upstream OPPORTUNITIES use LEGACY_CASE_ID 'IT-HERO-001..003' while canonical windows use LEGACY_CASE_ID 'IT-OPP-001..029'. There is no overlap, so the three real opportunities cannot currently be joined to a window by legacy id. Do not invent a join.

Deleting the fixture id (WIN-001 -> IT-WIN-0001) breaks any saved deep link and any hardcoded id in briefs, notifications or tests. The legacyId field plus a redirect in openWindow() is the cheap mitigation; skipping it will look like a routing bug.

D.WINDOW_KPI feeds the nav badge at line 2608 and today returns 29 by coincidence. If someone fixes the badge without fixing the badge's source, the number stays right for the wrong reason and the coupling survives the migration unnoticed.
openQuestions: Are the 10 D.OBSERVED rows (Consorzio Brunello harvest start, ERSA FVG BBCH 65-75, the Veneto and Umbria bulletin series) real observations from an earlier collection that simply never made it into ITALY_INGEST? If they are, the right fix is to promote them upstream into CROP_WINDOWS with dates and source ids, not to delete them — that would restore the observed dot on roughly 8 of 29 rows and is the single highest-value data question in this domain.

Is the empty PRODUCT_MATCHES array on all 29 canonical windows intentional (the audit deliberately keeps product linkage in ITALY_LABEL_VERDICTS) or is it an unfilled field? If it is meant to be filled, the model should prefer it over the verdicts join and the join becomes a fallback.

SOURCE_IDS is empty on all 29 windows. Should a window inherit the source ids of the regional regulatory act it joins (IT-SRC-REGIONAL, IT-SRC-PIEMONTE), or must a window's provenance stay strictly EXPECTED_NORM until the audit attaches its own sources?

WINDOW_TYPE is 'APPLICATION' for 29/29. Are MONITORING and REGULATORY window types planned as separate canonical records? If so, the calendar's monitoring and regulatory lanes should be built as row types now rather than as joined attributes of an application window.

D.PREP_LEAD is a single global 90 days for every crop, region and department. Is 90 a Sintonia planning convention that should be stated as such once, or a placeholder that the business owner intends to vary by crop? The interpretation label should name whichever it is.

Should the three regulatory acts whose region has no canonical window (Lombardia, Trentino, Emilia-Romagna Flavescenza) appear on the calendar as regulatory-only rows with no application window, or only in a separate list? They are real, dated, primary-source-backed facts and hiding them because the window audit has not caught up would be its own kind of loss.

summary: Two screens plus a cross-cutting relationship graph. PORTAFOGLIO (portale.html markup 1397-1424, logic 3026-3047) is already clean: it lists AM.products (166 = 163 real registrations + BUDGE/EXELGROW/PARLEAF which are catalog-only) in two deliberately separate tabs, CATALOGO COMMERCIALE (44 catalog items) and UNIVERSO REGOLATORIO (163 registrations), filtered by categoryLabel (ERBICIDI 91 / FUNGICIDI 46 / INSETTICIDI 23 / SPECIALI 6). PRODUCT INTELLIGENCE (markup 1339-1395, logic 2999-3023) shows one product's identity plus three relationship cards (verified / check-needed / not-confirmed) and a separate "VEDI OPPORTUNITÀ COLLEGATE" CTA. The identity facts are real (IG.PRODUCTS: name, reg, holder, ai, form, regCat, line, status, expiry, hrac/frac/irac, labelUrl — 163/163 populated). The RELATIONSHIPS are not: italy-app-model.js line 102 builds every product link by walking D.CASES[].productLinks, so which crop x issue x product triples exist at all is decided by a demo fixture (29 demo cases, 80 links). window.ITALY_LABEL_VERDICTS — the real 163-label audit — is loaded but italy-app-model.js never reads it; only italy-demo-data.js line 281 calls LV.verdict() to GRADE the fixture's own candidate list. The measured consequence: 57 distinct triples, of which 42 are LABEL_CHECK_NEEDED invented by the fixture; the visible 10 / 10 / 9 is the portfolioState of the 29 demo opportunity cards.

Product identity keeps coming from IG.PRODUCTS (163) joined to ITALY_CATALOG.ITEMS (44, matchState REGULATORY_MATCH_CONFIRMED 41 / NOT_FOUND 3). modelChanges.derivation: Iterate the 29 ITALY_CANONICAL.windows. TIER 1 CANONICAL: window.PRODUCT_MATCHES — MEASURED [] on all 29, so 0 rows today; keep the reader. TIER 2 LABEL_AUDIT: for each (crop, issue) match against ITALY_LABEL_VERDICTS.VERIFIED -> VERIFIED_LABEL_MATCH, and against .NOT_FOUND -> NO_CONFIRMED_MATCH_CURRENT_READING; needs an issue-alias table because the audit writes 'Cereal Aphids' and 'Cereal Aphids / BYDV Risk' where the window writes 'Cereal Aphids · BYDV Risk', and 'Diabrotica' where the window writes 'Diabrotica Adults'. Yields 14 verified rows and 15 not-confirmed rows across the 29 windows. TIER 3 REGULATORY_USE_ROW: IG.LINKS rows where LINK.crop is in CROP_KEY[window.CROP_NAME] and LINK.target matches ISSUE_TARGET[window.ISSUE_NAME], and the product was not already graded by tier 2 -> LABEL_CHECK_NEEDED. Yields 15 rows. TIER 4 CROP_REGISTRATION: IG.PRODUCTS where p.crops intersects CROP_KEY[window.CROP_NAME] AND p.line matches the window ISSUE_TYPE (PEST->INSETICIDA, DISEASE->FUNGICIDA, WEED->HERBICIDA), not already graded -> RELATED_PORTFOLIO. Yields 321 rows. WITHOUT the line gate this tier yields 1261 rows (a grapevine herbicide 'related' to Flavescenza Dorata) — the gate is mandatory.

risks: The rebuild's headline number gets WORSE, and that is the point. Window-level portfolio state goes from 10 VERIFIED / 10 LABEL_CHECK_NEEDED / 9 NO_CONFIRMED (measured today, on the 29 opportunity cards) to 12 VERIFIED / 6 LABEL_CHECK_NEEDED / 10 RELATED_PORTFOLIO / 1 NO_CONFIRMED. Verified goes UP (12 vs 10, because 4 audited verified triples were never reachable through the fixture and 2 fixture cards claimed verified without one), but 10 cards drop to the pale-blue RELATED_PORTFOLIO state and one card — Maize · Mycotoxin Risk, IT-WIN-0021 — ends with nothing at all, because no ADAMA fungicide is registered on maize in the 163 rows and 'Mycotoxin Risk' is not a label target. Anyone expecting the screen to get denser will read this as a regression.

The ISSUE_TARGET table is the one hand-authored input in the entire chain and it decides 15 of the 44 evidence-backed rows. If it is written loosely it manufactures matches; if it is written tightly it starves the check-needed class. It must be versioned, attributed, and surfaced per row via mappingRule — otherwise the rebuild replaces a demo fixture with an undocumented human judgement, which is the same defect wearing a better coat.

The RELATED_PORTFOLIO tier is enormous and low-value: 321 rows over 29 windows, with individual windows carrying up to 38 related products (Durum Wheat · Resistant grass weeds). It must be collapsed in the UI (a count plus a 'see all' link), never rendered as a list, or the screens become unreadable and the four-class hierarchy loses meaning.

Tier 1 is empty. The precedence 'HANDOFF V2.1 canonical > verified label verdict' is honoured in code but contributes nothing today: all 29 canonical windows have PRODUCT_MATCHES = []. Do not describe the result as canonical-backed. The strongest real evidence in the system is a 12-verified / 7-not-found audit of 163 labels, dated 2026-09-02, whose own SCOPE_NOTE says it verified the main visible claims and not every connection.

The label audit is small relative to the screens it governs: 19 audited triples against 29 windows and 166 products. Its NOT_FOUND set is 7 triples covering 6 products, and three of those seven are the same claim (Olive Fruit Fly) repeated across three windows — so a single audit row drives three cards to the palest state.

IG.LINKS covers 19 of 163 products. IG.CROPS states the gap explicitly and it is severe: GRAPEVINE has 61 products mentioning the crop and 1 with a use row read; DURUM_WHEAT has 14 and 0. Any check-needed count computed from use rows is a floor, not a measurement of the portfolio.

Deep links break. The competitor-product route ('cproduct') currently addresses 14 demo names; the real set is 36 different names. Old ids, bookmarks and any in-page chip pointing at Belanty/Revysol/Movento will 404 unless a fallback is added.

Four different ADAMA legal entities hold the 163 registrations (ADAMA ITALIA 85, ADAMA AGAN 35, ADAMA MAKHTESHIM 26, ADAMA DEUTSCHLAND 17) while the catalog is the Italian commercial site. Do not merge holder and seller into one 'ADAMA has this product' claim, and keep the two Portafoglio tabs separate — 41 of 44 catalog items match a registration, 3 (BUDGE, EXELGROW, PARLEAF, all SPECIALI) do not and are marked REGULATORY_MATCH_NOT_FOUND upstream.

15 of the 163 registrations have an expiry earlier than the 2026-09-02 reference date and 41 expire before 2027-01-01. Nothing in the current portfolio screens reads expiry. Surfacing a verified label match for an expired authorisation would be a new, avoidable false claim — worth guarding even though it is outside the strict scope of this migration.

D.CASES remains the source of the 29 opportunity objects even after relationships are rebuilt. This spec removes the demo from PRODUCT RELATIONSHIPS only; the opportunity/radar domain owner must handle the rest, and until then the relationship layer will be correct while the card it sits inside is still a scenario.
openQuestions: Is the ISSUE_TARGET mapping (English issue name -> Latin label target) acceptable as a Sintonia-authored artefact, or must it come from upstream? If it must come from upstream, tier 3 disappears and the result is 12 verified / 0 check-needed / 16 related / 1 no-confirmed across the 29 windows.

Should Durum Wheat inherit the WHEAT_GENERIC ('Frumento') use rows? DURUM_WHEAT itself has 0 use rows read. Inheriting adds check-needed candidates on two Durum Wheat windows; not inheriting leaves them related-only. This is an agronomic/regulatory call, not an engineering one.

Should RELATED_PORTFOLIO be gated more tightly than crop + product line? A tighter gate (e.g. same MoA family as an already-verified product) would cut the 321 rows sharply but adds another authored rule.
The 'region' line under each relationship card: relabel it as the window's region, or delete it? A label authorisation has no region.

Does the competitor-product view survive at all? IG.COMP_PRODUCTS has four fields. If crops/issues/dates cannot be derived from the 102 product-bearing activities, the view becomes a name, a company, an ad count and a proof string — which may be better folded into the company page than kept as its own route.

Is a fifth state (NOT_ASSESSED) acceptable alongside the four mandated strength classes, or must 'nothing has been looked at' be expressed as LABEL_CHECK_NEEDED? Collapsing it into LABEL_CHECK_NEEDED would put ~53 products and every unmatched triple into the amber class and re-inflate the number the rebuild is meant to deflate.

risks: Six of the twelve search groups (SOURCE, PEOPLE, COMPETITOR, EVENT, NEWS, and any science route through openTheme) land on screens that still resolve ids against the demo fixture with a `|| collection[0]` fallback. If the engineer wires them before those domains migrate, search becomes the fastest way in the whole product to reach a demo entity while believing it is real. The readiness gate is not optional polish — it is the safety mechanism for this change.

Search visibly gets emptier for some queries. Opportunity hits drop from 29 to 3; source hits from 53 to 31; researcher, source, company, event and news groups disappear entirely in phase 1. A reviewer who does not know the measurements will read this as a regression. Publish the before/after counts alongside the change.

The crop alias table is the one place in this spec where judgement enters the data path. Every entry must be a 1:1 lexical identity ('Zea mays' = 'Maize' = 'Mais'), never a semantic inference. 'CEREAL' → wheat, or 'cereali' → 'Frumento tenero', would be inventing a fact inside a lookup table, and it would be invisible in review because it lives in a synonym list rather than in a record.

Indexing all 503 competitor activities makes COMPETITOR the loudest group for almost any crop word (BASF alone has 138). With a 6-row cap and an honest '+497 more', the screen stays truthful, but the group ordering in SGROUP_DEF now decides what the user sees first. Put OPPORTUNITY, WINDOW and PRODUCT before COMPETITOR.

italy-app-model.js line 98 still admits D.PRODUCTS keys into `products` as SYNTHETIC_DEMO when they are absent from the registry and the catalog. Measured today: 0 such products, so nothing leaks. That is luck about the current data load, not a guarantee — the index push must still be guarded by !isDemo, or the next intelligence package silently puts demo product names into global search.

Fixing events.name, news.outlet, news.url, science.date, researchers.org and channels.url changes fields that other domains are reading right now as empty. Anything currently rendering a fallback dash for those will start rendering content, and anything that branched on the null (a `hasX` flag) will flip. Coordinate with the Archive, Sources and Science domains before landing step 3.

The Voci and GIRE focus highlight adds two new state keys and a border colour. Kept to that, it preserves the visual product. If it grows into a per-voice detail page it becomes a redesign, which §12 forbids in this pass.
openQuestions: Is there any appetite for a real per-voice detail screen? Today the Voci view is a flat list with no id anchor, so a voice search result can only scroll-and-highlight. That is honest but thin for 17 records that each carry a quote, a WHAT_IT_PROVES and a WHAT_IT_DOES_NOT_PROVE.

Which domain owns fixing the `|| collection[0]` fallbacks at portale.html 3171, 3181, 3185, 3367 and 3370? The signal view already has the correct pattern (sgMissing at 2892). Search cannot be made safe alone if those five keep silently substituting the first demo record.

Should channels (30) be their own search kind routed to Sources, or folded into the voice entries as extra terms? 17 voices carry a channel name; the other 13 channels have no voice. Folding loses 13 records, a separate kind needs a screen that lists real channels.

Market records CEREAL|'Feed barley' and CEREAL|'ORGFOUR|FEED' (8 observations) have no MK.CROPS bucket. Route them to Market Pulse with no crop preselected, or omit them from search until the market crop list covers barley?

italy-app-model.js never reads window.ITALY_LABEL_VERDICTS, so product link strengths still come from D.CASES[].productLinks (portale.html:102-105 in the model). domain: Helper relationships, visual tokens, Field Sales, reference date, localization
summary: This domain is the connective tissue: the colour/icon token tables (D.CAT, D.DEPT, D.F_COLOR, D.GROUP_COLOR, D.ATYPE_COLOR, D.STATUS), the formatting helpers (D.fmt, D.ago, D.inkOn, D.setMonths), the single clock (D.TODAY), the competitor crop axis (D.CROP_COLS), and the Field Sales inbound module (D.FIELD_MESSAGES, D.TSR, parseField/sendComposer/simulateInbound). Most of it really is presentation and can stay, but four pieces smuggle facts: D.CAT is not only colour and icon — its `label` ("Pest Control"/"Disease Control"/"Weed Control") is rendered as the big category chip via `catLabel` (portale.html:2450, markup 219 and 305), so every `|| D.CAT.disease` fallback (2819, 3139, 3207) prints a pest/disease/weed CLASSIFICATION that reality did not supply; D.F_COLOR is the enumeration of a 7-value future-signal status vocabulary that the real FUTURE_SIGNALS records do not have (measured: 3/3 real signals have status null, so all 7 filter chips count 0); D.GROUP_COLOR keys a source-group taxonomy that 31/31 real IG.SOURCES records lack (AM sources `group` is null 31/31); and D.FIELD_MESSAGES — 18 explicitly synthetic WhatsApp messages — is merged into `allMessages` (2603) and then rendered on two CORE screens: the Opportunity case panel "SEGNALI DI CAMPO · N" (2637, markup 403-408) and the Crop Windows "WHY PREPARE NOW?" reason row (2741, markup 764). Field Sales itself is correctly built as a separate INTEGRAZIONI · DEMO nav group, inbound only, with no phone number and no outbound send anywhere in the package. There is exactly one second clock: italy-briefs.js:119 calls `new Date()` for the brief timestamp. Italian is default and the language switch does not reload.
realSource: Visual tokens have no real source and do not need one — they move from window.ITALY_DEMO into a new AM.UI namespace in italy-app-model.js. The one fact they currently carry, the pest/disease/weed classification, comes from window.ITALY_CANONICAL.windows[].ISSUE_TYPE (measured 29/29 non-null: PEST 15, DISEASE 9, WEED 5) surfaced as AM.collections.windows.records[].issueType. The reference date comes from AM.referenceDate / AM.REF (2026-09-02, from ITALY_CANONICAL.meta.referenceDate). Localization comes from window.SINTONIA_I18N (371 keys, it + en both complete). Field Sales stays on AM.collections.fieldMessages (18 records, provenance SYNTHETIC_DEMO) but is confined to the isField screen. The competitor crop axis, if it survives, must come from IG.COMP_ACTIVITIES[].crops (Latin binomials plus Italian generics: Zea mays 67, Vitis vinifera 42, cereali 24, Olea europaea 24, colture 59, ... with 320/503 records carrying no crop at all).

Screens get emptier. §3 says a smaller truthful screen beats a dense fake one, and §12 says do not redesign to compensate — but someone will see the gap and ask for it to be filled. Have the answer ready before the edit lands.

Deleting the Future Radar status chip row leaves that screen with three real signals, no status, no category and a REGION that literally reads 'NAO SEI — o recorte cientifico e por afiliacao nacional, nao por regiao de estudo'. It will look broken. It is not broken; it is honest. That screen may need a deliberate empty-state, which is a design decision, not an engineering one.

AM.UI.CATEGORY.unknown has label:null and icon:''. Any markup binding that assumes a non-empty icon URL will render a broken image box. Lines 221, 287, 303, 756, 917, 1530, 1809, 2160, 2177, 2307, 2332 all bind category.icon — every one needs an sc-if guard, and it is easy to miss one.

D.DEPT currently has all six colours identical (#978B87). Moving to AM.UI.DEPARTMENT is a pure copy, so nothing changes visually — which means a mistake here is silent. Diff the rendered colours, do not trust the copy.

The competitor crop axis change is the highest-variance item. Swapping in real Latin binomials will change every number in the matrix, the density strip and the compMoments cards at once, and the demo-tuned HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW thresholds will misfire. Consider shipping the axis change behind the competitor spec's own review rather than as part of this one.
